recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future corrections to NPI identifier metadata should be handled through THO/TSMG rather than by changing FHIR core source; no follow-up core source work is needed for FHIR-7522.
issue_request: FHIR-7522 was a Published/Persuasive vocab change request from DSTU1 asking FHIR core to define a system URI for OID 2.16.840.1.113883.4.6, the US National Provider Identifier. The Jira resolution was approve as edited, with a later Jira comment noting that the work was already done.
initial_application: No commit explicitly mentions FHIR-7522. The same NPI URI request was applied through companion issue FHIR-8047 in svn revision 6064, represented by git commit c8797d9ce12b17c991437850da507680fa9e7a45, which added the old in-core NamingSystem registry entry for United States National Provider Identifier with preferred URI http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/us-npi and OID 2.16.840.1.113883.4.6.
additional_context: FHIR-8047 is already represented on the combined branch by audit commit 490bdb506cd63a698e3fb92d7b483498e6e2fc93, so this worker did not publish a duplicate FHIR-8047 commit. FHIR-37889 later removed the old in-core NamingSystem registry bundles because identifier and terminology registry content is authoritatively maintained in HL7 Terminology. Current core source keeps identifier-registry.html in the build hierarchy and directs implementers to terminology.hl7.org for active identifier systems. The current THO package contains NamingSystem/npi with the requested OID and preferred URI, and current core examples use http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/us-npi.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit for FHIR-7522. No source edit is appropriate because NPI is an Identifier.system rather than a Coding system for terminologies-systems.html, and restoring the old in-core NamingSystem entry would contradict the later FHIR-37889 migration to THO.

related_jiras.note: Companion Published/Persuasive issue that named the resolved URI http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/us-npi and was explicitly referenced by the original application commit; already audited on the combined branch.
Published/Persuasive later decision that removed the in-core NamingSystem registry bundles in favor of authoritative THO content, explaining why the old NPI entry should not be restored.
Non-final terminology request about improving the CMS link for the THO NPI identifier; it does not require or authorize a core source change.
